rationale:
TRIAGE: All three candidates merit head-to-head downstream comparison because they represent two distinct endpoint definitions and two within-publication sibling models where a single-shot picker could be misled.

- PGS001033 is the only candidate directly aligned to the target trait EFO label (“blood coagulation disease”) and reports clean, comparable discrimination metrics including PRS-only AUROC/R² plus full-model AUROC with conventional covariates. It also has a much larger validation N (n=67,425) and multi-ancestry evaluation distribution (though the selected performance shown is European). This makes it a strong direct-endpoint anchor even if it is a different reported phenotype string (“Other coagulation defects (time-to-event)”).

- PGS001826 and PGS002034 share the same reported phenotype (“Congenital deficiency of other clotting factors…”) and come from the same portability study with identical training size, validation size, ancestry mix, and covariate set. Their reported performance is partial correlation (partial-r) rather than AUROC/R², which is cleaner as a PRS-focused metric but not directly comparable to PGS001033’s AUROC. Because they are siblings with near-identical partial-r (0.0562 vs 0.0563) but very different variant counts (45 vs 32,552) and different methods (penalized regression vs LDpred2), they are a classic near-tie where picking based on method label or variant count alone could mislead; both should be kept for direct comparison.

Downstream comparison should explicitly separate (a) endpoint fidelity to the target trait label (PGS001033 vs the congenital-deficiency endpoint) from (b) within-endpoint model choice (PGS001826 vs PGS002034), and avoid over-weighting metric-type cleanliness since the metric families differ across these two endpoint clusters. Uncertainty: Key uncertainty is comparability across metric types: PGS001033 provides AUROC/R² (PRS-only and full-model), while PGS001826/PGS002034 provide partial-r only, making cross-cluster performance comparison indirect. Another uncertainty is endpoint alignment: PGS001033’s “other coagulation defects (TTE)” may not match the congenital-deficiency endpoint captured by PGS001826/PGS002034, so downstream PICK must decide whether direct EFO alignment and AUROC evidence outweigh the alternative endpoint specificity and portability-study context. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All three candidates are direct matches at the broad level of “blood coagulation disease” via coagulation-defect phenotypes, but none is a clean, high-confidence choice given the visible metadata. PGS001033 maps directly to the target EFO (“blood coagulation disease”) and provides PRS-comparable discrimination metrics including PGS-only AUROC (0.634) and PGS R² (0.0578), with basic covariates and multi-ancestry evaluation; however, it is from a pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-score framework (“across 813 traits”) and is extremely sparse (1 variant) with a time-to-event endpoint, both of which are warning signals for generalizability. The two alternatives (PGS001826, PGS002034) are for a narrower congenital clotting-factor deficiency EFO (not the broad target EFO) and come from a UKB portability framework with only partial-correlation metrics (no AUROC/R²), making them hard to compare and also framework-penalized; between them, PGS002034 has a much larger variant count (32,552 vs 45) but otherwise near-identical evidence. Given the target is broad and only PGS001033 is explicitly aligned to the target EFO with PRS-comparable metrics, it is the best-supported direct-match in this context, but confidence remains low due to framework origin and endpoint/method limitations. PICK: Keeping the legacy proposal is still defensible on the visible evidence. Among the three candidates, PGS001033 is the only record whose trait_efo exactly matches the target trait label (“blood coagulation disease”), and it also provides directly comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.634; full-model AUROC 0.656 with conventional covariates; plus PRS-only R²). It is trained at large scale (n=269,704) and has a larger reported validation sample size (n=67,425) than the alternatives.

PGS001826 and PGS002034 are direct matches only at a narrower congenital clotting-factor-deficiency endpoint (different EFO than the target) and report only partial correlation (~0.056) rather than AUROC/R², making cross-candidate predictive comparison weaker/less interpretable here. Between those two siblings, PGS002034 is a marginally stronger runner-up (slightly higher partial-r and much broader variant coverage), but neither shows stronger overall predictive evidence than PGS001033 across multiple independent visible axes.

Confidence remains low because PGS001033 comes from a broad pan-trait UKB framework and uses a time-to-event phenotype with an extremely sparse model (1 variant), which are generalizability/robustness warning signals even though the endpoint label alignment and metric reporting are the best among the candidates. CRITIC: No visible contradiction found with keeping PGS001033 as the pick. It is the only candidate whose trait_efo exactly matches the target trait label (“blood coagulation disease”), and it is also the only record providing directly comparable discrimination metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.634 with CI; full-model AUROC 0.656 with conventional covariates; PRS-only R² 0.0578) plus a larger validation sample size (n=67,425). The alternatives (PGS001826, PGS002034) target a narrower/different EFO (“congenital vitamin K-dependent coagulation factors deficiency”) and report only partial correlation (~0.056) without AUROC/R², making them less directly supported for this target on the visible evidence. Between those two siblings, PGS002034 is a reasonable runner-up (slightly higher partial-r; different method/variant count), but not better-supported overall than PGS001033 given endpoint/EFO alignment and richer performance reporting. The noted weaknesses for PGS001033 (pan-trait UKB framework, time-to-event phenotype, extremely sparse 1-variant model) are real caution flags but do not create a concrete visible reason to revise away from it, and the legacy_with_domain_proposal matches the proposed_pick, so no reversion change applies.

TRIAGE: All three candidates are direct-endpoint Crohn’s disease scores and should be kept for close downstream comparison.

- PGS004254: Stands out on reported discrimination (AUROC 0.72 with tight CI) and includes an effect size (OR 2.18). However, the metric appears to be reported as a full model AUROC (no PRS-only AUC/R² shown), so it could be misleading in a single-shot pick if covariates contribute materially; it deserves head-to-head checking against the UKB snpnet siblings on comparable axes.

- PGS001331 vs PGS001330 (same publication family, similar covariates/validation N): Near-tie siblings with clean PRS-only metrics available. PGS001331 is slightly stronger on both PRS-only AUROC/R² and full-model AUROC/incremental AUROC, but differences are small enough that endpoint definition differences matter.

- Endpoint-definition trap to preserve for downstream: PGS001330 is explicitly time-to-event (TTE) Crohn’s disease [regional enteritis], while PGS001331 is a non-TTE Crohn’s disease label. Depending on the intended endpoint/horizon, either could be the better-aligned choice even if the other has marginally higher AUC.

Given these trade-offs (strong but potentially packaged metric in PGS004254; near-tie clean-metric siblings with differing endpoint framing), all three warrant close comparison rather than early elimination. Uncertainty: PGS004254’s headline AUROC may not be PRS-only and could reflect covariate contribution; the records don’t show PRS-only AUC/R² for it. For PGS001330 vs PGS001331, the practical impact of TTE vs non-TTE phenotyping on downstream use is unclear from the metadata alone, and the performance differences are small. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All three candidates are direct matches to Crohn disease by trait_efo and phenotyping_reported. PGS001330 is a time-to-event endpoint (explicit warning signal vs generic disease risk) and comes from a pan-trait UK Biobank framework paper (“across 813 traits”), with modest PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC ~0.576; PGS R2 ~0.006). PGS001331 is also from the same pan-trait framework family but uses a straightforward Crohn’s disease endpoint and shows slightly better PRS-only performance than PGS001330 (PGS AUROC ~0.579; PGS R2 ~0.0068; incremental AUROC ~0.027). PGS004254 is endpoint-aligned (Crohn’s disease), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) with far more variants (744,682), and reports strong discrimination/effect evidence in European validation (AUROC 0.72 with CI 0.70–0.73; OR 2.18 per SD), with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs). Main limitation: the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (no explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 provided), making cross-model metric comparability imperfect; nonetheless, the combination of endpoint fidelity, method/variant coverage, and strong effect-size evidence supports selecting PGS004254 over the two pan-trait sparse snpnet scores. PICK: Legacy proposal (PGS004254) remains defensible after inspecting all candidates. All three are direct matches on trait_efo (Crohn disease) and phenotyping_reported, but PGS004254 shows substantially stronger visible predictive evidence in its evaluation: AUROC 0.72 with tight CI (0.70–0.73) plus an OR 2.18 (2.05–2.32), with conventional covariates (age, sex, PCs) and a large-variant LDpred2-auto genome-wide score. While its AUROC is not explicitly labeled PRS-only (so metric packaging comparability vs the snpnet UKB siblings is imperfect), there is no visible indication of unusual/leaky covariate packaging, and the magnitude/tightness of the discrimination/effect evidence is markedly stronger than PGS001331/PGS001330 (PRS-only AUROC ~0.58; full-model AUROC ~0.61; small incremental AUROC). Between the two snpnet siblings, PGS001331 is the cleaner runner-up for a non–time-to-event Crohn’s disease endpoint and slightly better metrics than PGS001330, but neither is competitively supported against PGS004254 on the visible performance axes. CRITIC: No visible contradiction found with keeping PGS004254 as best. All candidates are direct matches on trait_efo=Crohn disease and phenotyping_reported/trait_reported. PGS004254 has markedly stronger visible evaluation evidence (AUROC 0.72, CI 0.70–0.73; OR 2.18, CI 2.05–2.32) in EUR validation (n=22,296) with conventional covariates (age, sex, 10 PCs) and a genome-wide LDpred2-auto model (744,682 variants). The main caveat is metric packaging: the AUROC is shown as full_model_auc with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so strict comparability vs the snpnet siblings’ PRS-only AUC (~0.576–0.579) is imperfect; however, there is no visible sign of unusual/leaky covariates, and the magnitude/tight CI plus OR provide stronger predictive evidence than PGS001331/PGS001330 (full-model AUROC ~0.603–0.613; incremental AUROC ~0.024–0.027; PRS-only AUROC ~0.58). Between the snpnet siblings, PGS001331 is slightly stronger than PGS001330 and avoids the explicit time-to-event framing present in PGS001330, but neither is better-supported than PGS004254 on the visible performance axes. The legacy_with_domain_proposal also selected PGS004254, so no revision back is applicable.

TRIAGE: Cluster the 8 candidates into two publication families with different endpoint framing and evaluation contexts, then keep representatives from each for head-to-head comparison.

1) 2024-12-16 Nat Genet family (PGS004946–PGS004951): these provide PRS-only discrimination metrics (univariate PRS-only AUC and AUPRC) plus delta-R2 style increments, which are especially useful for downstream apples-to-apples comparison across siblings.
- Keep the strongest MTAG and non-MTAG siblings with the clearest PRS-only signal: PGS004949 (non-ischemic DCM, MTAG; PRS-only AUC 0.68; strong OR) and PGS004951 (clinical DCM, MTAG; PRS-only AUC 0.67; strong OR). These are plausible near-ties but differ in endpoint label (non-ischemic vs clinical) and validation scale (large MAE eval vs small EUR eval), which could mislead a single-shot picker.
- Keep additional near-tie comparators within the same family: PGS004947 (non-ischemic DCM, MTAG; PRS-only AUC 0.66) and PGS004946 (non-ischemic DCM, non-MTAG; PRS-only AUC 0.65). These help disentangle whether MTAG vs non-MTAG and small AUC differences are stable or just endpoint/validation-context artifacts.
- Put PGS004950 (clinical DCM, non-MTAG; PRS-only AUC 0.64; very small validation n=7,761) on watchlist: it is a clean PRS-only-metric sibling but could look deceptively weaker due to the much smaller evaluation set and different endpoint packaging; still worth retaining as a “cleaner but potentially underpowered” comparator.
- Put PGS004948 (non-ischemic DCM, non-MTAG; PRS-only AUC 0.64) on watchlist as a weaker sibling that can still be informative for sensitivity checks within the same study family.

2) 2024-04-18 Nat Genet family (PGS004861–PGS004862): these are direct DCM labels with very large EUR validation (n=347,585) but report performance primarily as full-model AUROC/R2 (with conventional covariates) rather than PRS-only AUC/R2.
- Keep both PGS004862 (MTAG; full-model AUROC 0.71; OR 1.76) and PGS004861 (non-MTAG; full-model AUROC 0.70; OR 1.56) on the shortlist as “clean covariate, huge validation N” alternatives that could be competitive despite less perfectly separated PRS-only reporting. They also provide an internal MTAG vs non-MTAG comparison under a consistent evaluation framework.

Overall downstream comparison should explicitly account for (a) endpoint wording differences (dilated vs non-ischemic vs clinical), (b) MTAG vs non-MTAG siblings, (c) PRS-only vs full-model metric reporting, and (d) large differences in validation sample size/ancestry context that could make one record look better or worse for reasons unrelated to the underlying score quality. Uncertainty: Key uncertainty is metric comparability across the two publication families: PGS004861/PGS004862 lack PRS-only AUC/R2 in the visible fields, while the 2024-12-16 family provides PRS-only AUC/AUPRC and delta-R2. Also, several 2024-12-16 records evaluate in MAE-only or small EUR samples, so apparent performance differences among siblings (and versus the 2024-04-18 family) may reflect evaluation context and endpoint framing rather than intrinsic score superiority. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All 8 candidates are direct matches to the target trait (dilated cardiomyopathy) by trait_reported/trait_efo, with phenotyping_reported spanning generic DCM, non-ischemic DCM, and clinical DCM. Per the provided domain knowledge, endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported) is primary and MTAG variants are mildly preferred over non-MTAG siblings when the disease endpoint remains the same. Among the MTAG models, PGS004951 is a clinical dilated cardiomyopathy endpoint (closest to the generic disease concept) and shows the strongest visible discriminative evidence within that clinical-endpoint pair (full-model AUROC 0.67; OR 1.93) compared with its non-MTAG sibling PGS004950 (AUROC 0.64; OR 1.71). While some non-ischemic MTAG models report higher liability-scale R² values, those are not clearly PRS-only metrics and are evaluated in a different ancestry context (EVAL: MAE 100%) and a narrower phenotype (non-ischemic), making cross-candidate metric comparability and endpoint alignment less clean. Confidence is moderated because none of the candidates provides an explicit PRS-only AUROC/R², and several models come from different study families/endpoints with non-comparable reported metrics. PICK: Keep the legacy pick. PGS004951 remains a defensible best-supported direct match because it targets a directly aligned endpoint label (phenotyping_reported: “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy”), uses conventional covariates (Sex, PC1-12; no obvious packaging/leakage signals), and shows strong visible predictive evidence within its closest sibling comparison: versus the non-MTAG clinical sibling PGS004950 it has higher PRS-only AUC (0.67 vs 0.64), higher full-model AUROC (0.67 vs 0.64), and higher OR (1.93 vs 1.71), consistent with a stronger score under the same endpoint framing and evaluation context.

There are two credible challengers but neither is clearly better across multiple independent axes while staying at least as endpoint-direct:

- PGS004862 (Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG), very large EUR validation n=347,585) reports higher full-model AUROC (0.71) than PGS004951, but it does not provide PRS-only AUC/R² in the visible fields, making it harder to attribute the discrimination specifically to the PRS rather than the conventional covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs). Its OR (1.76) is also lower than PGS004951’s (1.93). Net: strong alternative with excellent validation scale, but not a clearly superior PRS on the visible evidence.

- PGS004949 (Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG), large validation n=326,106) has the highest PRS-only AUC among candidates (0.68) and a strong OR (1.91), but its endpoint is explicitly narrower (“Non-ischemic”), so it is slightly less direct to the generic target trait than the clinical DCM endpoint. Given the small AUC difference and the endpoint narrowing, this is not enough to overturn the legacy choice.

Thus, no revision is warranted: PGS004951 best balances direct endpoint alignment with strong, explicitly PRS-only discrimination/effect evidence among the clinical-DCM candidates. CRITIC: No visible contradiction found with keeping PGS004951. It is a direct match on trait_reported/trait_efo and has endpoint wording closest to the generic target among the 2024-12-16 family (phenotyping_reported: “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy”). Within its closest like-for-like sibling (same endpoint framing, same EUR eval context, same covariates), PGS004951 is consistently stronger than PGS004950: higher univariate PRS-only AUC (0.67 vs 0.64), higher full-model AUROC (0.67 vs 0.64), and higher OR (1.93 vs 1.71). That is strong visible internal evidence.

Challengers:
- PGS004862 has higher full-model AUROC (0.71) and huge EUR validation n=347,585, but lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 in visible fields and uses additional conventional covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs), so the incremental PRS contribution is less directly evidenced; its OR (1.76) is also lower than PGS004951’s 1.93.
- PGS004949 shows the highest PRS-only AUC (0.68) with large validation n=326,106 and strong OR (1.91), but its phenotyping_reported is explicitly narrower (“Non-ischemic dilated cardiomyopathy”), making endpoint alignment to the generic target slightly less direct than “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy.” The small AUC edge is not a clear enough visible basis to overturn endpoint fidelity.

Legacy proposal equals proposed_pick (PGS004951), and it remains more defensible than switching given the visible endpoint alignment + PRS-only evidence + sibling dominance and no packaging/leakage red flags in covariates.

TRIAGE: Downstream comparison should explicitly separate (a) direct/near-direct endpoint alignment and (b) metric packaging differences (PRS-only vs full-model) so a single-shot picker isn’t misled by “better-looking” but non-comparable metrics.

Shortlist rationale (close head-to-head):
- MVP CHF PheCode 428.1 family with strong reported discrimination (C-index ~0.74–0.754) and ORs often ~1.44–1.46: PGS005083/PGS005077/PGS005084/PGS005076/PGS005078 plus the closely similar PRS-CS sibling PGS005080 and PRS-CSx PGS005085. These are near-ties within one study family; small metric differences could be noise or cohort/packaging artifacts, so they deserve direct comparison rather than picking the numerically top one.
- PGS005074 is included as a near-tie anchor within the same MVP family (high C-index ~0.752; OR ~1.43) and helps check whether ldpred vs prscs variants are materially different.
- PGS001790 (GBMI, PRS-CS-auto) has clean PRS-only R2 reported (Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out) plus a full-model AUROC 0.75 in a very large EUR evaluation (n~359k). Even though the AUROC is full-model, the presence of a PRS-only metric makes it a key “clean-metric” comparator against the MVP family.
- PGS005097 (Nat Genet 2025, PRS-CSx) is directly labeled heart failure with AUROC ~0.72 (full-model) and additional calibration-type evidence (Brier skill score). Endpoint is prevalent HF; still strong enough and recent enough to compare against MVP/GBMI.
- PGS000709 (UKB snpnet multi-PRS) is directly labeled heart failure with time-to-event framing (C-index 0.635; HR per unit ~1.08) and large validation N. Metrics are not directly comparable to case-control AUROC/C-index from other families, but it’s a plausible “different modeling frame” candidate that could mislead if excluded.

Watchlist rationale (plausible alternatives / misleading evidence risks):
- Commun Biol 2024 I50 HF scores (PGS004532 metaPRS; PGS004462 LDpred2) report only ORs with unknown covariates/packaging; could look strong (OR ~1.27 for metaPRS) but may not be comparable and may embed risk-factor integration. Keep for later scrutiny.
- Sparse-variant GWS scores (PGS003969, PGS005319, PGS004598) can show decent OR/HR but may underperform genome-wide PRS; still worth retaining because they are direct endpoint (or incident HF) and sometimes more portable/robust.
- Remaining MVP CHF siblings (PGS005073/PGS005079/PGS005082/PGS005075/PGS005081) are close to the shortlisted MVP set but slightly weaker on the visible metrics; keep to avoid overfitting to tiny metric deltas.
- NPJ Genom Med 2025 LDpred2 cluster (PGS005299–PGS005306) has multiple siblings with modest AUROC (~0.57–0.63) and R2; endpoints are prevalent HF with smaller validation Ns. These could be “clean but weaker” comparators and help sanity-check whether the MVP/GBMI results are unusually high due to phenotype/covariate packaging.
- UKB portability CHF/nonhypertensive and pulmonary heart disease scores (PGS001842/PGS002051 and PGS001840/PGS002049) are not exact endpoint matches but are adjacent labels with partial-r metrics across ancestries; keep as potential portability-focused alternatives, but not primary for direct HF picking. Uncertainty: Many candidates report full-model discrimination (often with age/sex/PCs) rather than PRS-only metrics, making cross-family comparisons non-like-for-like. The MVP family contains many near-duplicate records with very small C-index differences; without more detail on phenotype definition, outcome horizon, and whether metrics are PRS-only vs covariate-augmented, the apparent ordering among them is uncertain. Several records have ‘Unknown’ covariates and/or only OR/HR without clear scaling, which could inflate perceived strength or hinder comparability. LEGACY_PROPOSAL: All listed candidates are direct/near-direct matches to the target (heart failure), but the evidence is heterogeneous and often not PRS-comparable (many report only full-model AUROC/C-index or partial correlation, and several have unknown covariates), which prevents a clearly high-confidence pick. PGS005097 is preferred because it has strong phenotype alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo = heart failure; phenotyping_reported = prevalent heart failure), comes from a clearly disease-focused heart-failure genetics study with broad multi-cohort development (BBJ, BioMe, CKB, FinnGen, GBMI, HERMES, MVP, etc.), uses a methodologically strong genome-wide shrinkage/transfer approach (PRS-CSx) with large variant count (1,274,692), and reports discrimination (AUROC 0.72 with CI) plus an additional metric (Brier skill score 0.065). The main limitation is that the reported AUROC appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only) and covariates are present (age, sex, PCs), making cross-model performance comparisons imperfect; additionally, some competing CHF models (e.g., PGS005077/PGS005083) report slightly higher C-index (~0.754) but are from a methods-comparison framework context with less endpoint-specific study focus visible here, so the superiority is not decisive from the provided metadata. PICK: Revising the legacy pick (PGS005097) is defensible because multiple independent visible axes favor the top-performing MVP CHF (PheCode 428.1) models over PGS005097 on predictive evidence while remaining a near-direct endpoint match to heart failure.

Why PGS005083 over the legacy PGS005097:
- Endpoint alignment: Both are essentially direct matches to the target trait (heart failure). PGS005083 is labeled “Congestive heart failure (CHF), NOS” (congestive HF is a close/near-synonymous clinical endpoint family for HF), while PGS005097 is “Prevalent heart failure.” Neither is an obvious mismatch.
- Stronger visible discrimination: PGS005083 reports C-index 0.75368 (European validation), which is visibly higher than PGS005097’s AUROC 0.72 (also appears to be full-model). While AUROC vs C-index are not perfectly interchangeable, both are discrimination metrics and the gap is large enough to matter as visible evidence.
- Stronger visible effect size: PGS005083 reports OR 1.455 (1.38–1.54), compared with PGS005097 which does not show an OR/HR in the record. This provides an additional independent axis of predictive signal for PGS005083.
- Comparable covariate packaging: PGS005083 uses ordinary covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs). PGS005097 also uses ordinary covariates (age, sex, 5 PCs). Neither appears to embed unusual clinical-risk-factor packaging in the covariates as shown.

Why PGS005083 among the MVP CHF family:
- It is the strongest on the visible metrics within that near-duplicate set: highest reported C-index (0.75368) and highest reported OR (1.455) among the listed MVP CHF candidates, edging out very close siblings (e.g., PGS005077/PGS005084).

Why not pick other direct HF-labeled alternatives:
- PGS001790 has very large EUR validation (n=358,905) and a PRS-only Nagelkerke R2 (0.006981), but its reported AUROC 0.75 is full-model and it lacks an effect-size axis in the record; overall, it does not clearly surpass the MVP top model on the combined visible evidence.
- PGS005097 remains strong (multi-cohort HF-focused study context; AUROC with CI; Brier skill score), but its discrimination is lower than the best MVP CHF models in the visible record.
- Other HF records either have weaker discrimination (e.g., PGS000709 C-index 0.635; NPJ Genom Med 2025 cluster AUROC ~0.57–0.63) or have limited/unclear performance packaging (e.g., OR-only with unknown covariates).

Net: PGS005083 is a near-direct HF endpoint score with the strongest combined visible predictive evidence (discrimination + effect size) and conventional covariate adjustment, making it the best-supported direct-match choice from the full candidate list. CRITIC: No visible contradiction that would force revising away from the proposed pick PGS005083, and the legacy pick PGS005097 is not more defensible on the visible evidence.

Visible evidence supporting keeping PGS005083:
- Endpoint alignment: PGS005083 is labeled “Congestive heart failure (CHF), NOS (PheCode 428.1)” with trait_efo “congestive heart failure”, which is a near-direct match to the target “heart failure” and is closer than clearly different endpoints (e.g., pulmonary heart disease/cor pulmonale).
- Predictive evidence: Among the MVP CHF family shown, PGS005083 has the strongest combined visible discrimination + effect size: C-index 0.75368 and OR 1.455 (1.38–1.54). Close siblings are slightly lower (e.g., PGS005077 C-index 0.75358 OR 1.452; PGS005084 C-index 0.75272 OR 1.45; PGS005080 C-index 0.75317 OR 1.44).
- Packaging/covariates: Covariates are conventional (age, sex, 20 PCs) and do not visibly indicate unusual clinical-risk-factor packaging.

Why not revert to legacy PGS005097:
- PGS005097 is also a direct HF label (“Heart failure”; phenotyping “Prevalent heart failure”) and has good study context plus AUROC 0.72 (CI) and Brier skill score 0.065, but it does not show an effect size in the record and its discrimination is not visibly stronger than the MVP CHF top models.
- The proposed rationale’s comparison caveat (AUROC vs C-index not identical) is valid, but there is no visible evidence that would make PGS005097 clearly superior overall.

Checks against other visible alternatives:
- PGS001790 has very large EUR validation and a PRS-only Nagelkerke R2 (0.006981) plus full-model AUROC 0.75, but lacks an effect-size axis in the record and does not clearly exceed PGS005083 on the combined visible evidence.
- PGS000709 has much lower C-index (0.635) despite large N.
- OR-only records with unknown covariates (PGS004532/PGS004462) are less well-supported for a primary pick given missing discrimination and unclear packaging.

Therefore, keeping PGS005083 is defensible, and there is no concrete visible basis to revise back to PGS005097.

TRIAGE: Shortlist focuses on candidates with (a) direct hip OA / coxarthrosis endpoints and (b) some comparable predictive evidence (AUC/C-index/HR/OR) and/or strong validation scale.

- PGS000967: Direct hip coxarthrosis TTE endpoint; reports both PRS-only AUROC/R² and full-model AUROC with conventional covariates. This is the cleanest PRS-only-metric anchor for head-to-head comparison, despite modest PRS-only AUROC.
- PGS002728: Hip OA framed via total hip replacement; has an AUROC with CI (age/sex covariates). Endpoint is a proxy/advanced-disease definition that can look stronger/weaker depending on comparison, so it deserves direct comparison rather than being dropped.
- PGS004882: Incident hip OA with very large validation N and time-to-event framing (C-index + HR). Metrics aren’t PRS-only and training sample size is unusual/unclear (n=404 with 1000G listed), but the validation scale and direct incident endpoint could dominate; also a candidate whose evidence could mislead a single-shot picker if not scrutinized.
- PGS002763: Direct hip OA endpoint with very large variant count (PRS-CS) and a relatively strong OR with CI in a sizable validation sample. Lacks AUC/C-index, but the effect-size evidence is strong enough to keep as a near-tie contender.

Watchlist keeps plausible alternatives and “sibling” models where limited/unclear metric packaging could otherwise cause over- or under-selection:
- PGS004478 vs PGS004548: Same publication family, same endpoint label (M16 coxarthrosis) and same variant count; only ORs shown and covariates unknown. They should be compared against each other (and against the shortlist) because one could be preferable depending on what the hidden evaluation setup was.
- PGS002750: Total hip replacement endpoint with OR+CI but very small validation N and heavier covariate set; could look compelling from OR alone yet be unstable/less comparable, so keep for downstream scrutiny rather than exclude. Uncertainty: Key comparability gaps: several candidates lack PRS-only metrics (AUC/R²) and/or omit covariates (PGS004478/PGS004548), making it unclear whether reported OR/HR reflect PRS-only or packaged models. Endpoint heterogeneity (incident hip OA vs coxarthrosis code vs total hip replacement) can invert apparent performance.
